title: Tuning the magneto–electrocatalytic activity of molybdenum disulphide through Sn doping as an efficient bifunctional electrocatalyst
content: Beyond traditional structural and compositional engineering, magnetic-field-assisted electrocatalysis has emerged as a promising approach for accelerating water-splitting kinetics. In this study, we investigate the effect of an external static magnetic field (0–2000 G) on the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activities of pristine 2H–MoS2 and Sn-modified MoS2. Among the investigated compositions, MS-10, with a nominal Sn : (Mo + Sn) molar ratio of 10%, exhibits the optimum electrocatalytic performance. While pristine MoS2 shows a comparatively limited response to the applied magnetic field, the Sn-modified catalyst demonstrates a pronounced enhancement in both HER and OER activity under magnetic stimulation. At 2000 G, substantial reductions in overpotential are observed for both reactions, accompanied by marked decreases in Tafel slope and polarization resistance, as evidenced by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. The increase in double-layer capacitance under magnetic stimulation further indicates enhanced electrochemically accessible surface area. Complementary DFT calculations reveal that Sn incorporation modifies the electronic structure of MoS2 by introducing additional electronic states near the Fermi level and reducing the band gap, providing an electronic basis for the experimentally observed enhancement. Furthermore, the calculated HER and OER overpotentials of Sn-decorated MoS2 are lower than those of pristine MoS2, demonstrating the favourable role of Sn in facilitating the corresponding electrochemical reactions. The combined experimental and theoretical results highlight the synergistic contribution of Sn-induced electronic modification and magnetic-field-induced magnetohydrodynamic effects, establishing Sn-modified MoS2 as a promising platform for magnetic-field-enhanced bifunctional water-splitting electrocatalysis.
